name: @polypad/mcp

tools.name: new_project
tools.description: Start a new, empty Polypad project (optionally from a template), after saving the open one (it stays in the projects list: list_projects, open_project). All lengths in Polypad are millimetres and angles are degrees; Z is up.

template.description: Start from a template (spacer: A round spacer or washer: outer and inner diameter and height. bracket: An L-shaped bracket: leg length, material thickness and width. enclosure: A box with a lid whose lip fits inside: size, wall thickness and clearance.). Omit for an empty project.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the projects saved in this browser (name, id, number of features, when last saved, which one is open), newest first. Use open_project to go back to one.

tools.name: open_project
tools.description: Open a project saved in this browser (its id is listed by list_projects), after saving the open one. Nothing is lost; call get_project afterwards to see the project that is open now.

id.description: Id of the project to open (from list_projects)

tools.name: set_parameter
tools.description: Create or change a named parameter (a number or an expression). Any length field of any feature can use the name, so one change resizes everything bound to it. Reports features that no longer build. Set the sizes up front, then use the names in fields.

name.description: Parameter name: letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit. Created when it does not exist yet.

value.description: Value in mm (or degrees where it is used as an angle), a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1". Other fields can refer to the parameter by name.

tools.name: add_primitive
tools.description: Add a solid box, cylinder, tube, sphere, cone, torus or wedge as a new body. Returns the new feature's id, which is also the body id for later commands. Sizes in mm. A cylinder, cone, tube or torus can lie along X or Y with `axis`.

width.description: Size along X, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

depth.description: Size along Y, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

height.description: Size along Z, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

radius.description: Radius, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

height.description: Height along the axis (Z unless `axis` says otherwise), in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

radius.description: Radius, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"
Radius of the base, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

topRadius.description: Radius of the top in mm, 0 for a point, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

height.description: Height along the axis (Z unless `axis` says otherwise), in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

radius.description: Outer radius, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

innerRadius.description: Inner radius, smaller than the outer radius, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

height.description: Height along the axis (Z unless `axis` says otherwise), in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

radius.description: Distance from the centre to the middle of the ring's tube, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

tubeRadius.description: Radius of the tube, smaller than the ring radius, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

width.description: Size of the base along X, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

depth.description: Size along Y, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

height.description: Height along Z, at the tall side, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

topWidth.description: Width of the flat top in mm, 0 for a sharp ramp edge, the width for a box, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

shape.description: The solid to add. A primitive stands on the XY plane: its base is centred on `position` and it grows upwards along Z. A torus stands on the XY plane too (it spans z 0 to twice its tube radius). A wedge is tallest at its -X side and slopes down to +X; its top is `topWidth` wide.

axis.description: Which way a cylinder, cone, tube or torus stands: "z" (the default) upright, "x" or "y" laid along that axis, so you never need to work out rotation signs. The base centre stays at `position` and the body grows towards +X or +Y (a torus has its ring around that axis). When `position` is left out, the body rests on the grid at the origin (its lowest point on z = 0), whatever the axis. When `position` is given, it is the base centre and `axis` only sets the rotation, so a cylinder of radius 5 laid along X at z = 0 sinks 5 mm below the grid: give z = 5 to rest it. Not for box, sphere or wedge, and not together with `rotation`. get_project and measure report it as `axis`.

position.description: Where the centre of the base goes. Omitted: the origin, with the lowest point of the body on z = 0: [x, y, z] in mm. Z is up.

rotation.description: Rotation about X, then Y, then Z, around the base centre (omit it when you use `axis`): [x, y, z] in degrees. Z is up.

tools.name: list_parts
tools.description: List the standard parts in the library (boards, servos, motors, batteries, fans, displays and more): id, name, size, screws and mounting holes, ports, variants, and whether the size is only typical. Filter by group or search words. Add one to the project with add_part.

group.description: Only this group: boards, motors, power, fans, displays-sensors, connectors-switches or hardware

search.description: Words to find in the name, id, tags or variants, e.g. "raspberry", "nema", "m3"

tools.name: add_part
tools.description: Add a standard part (a board, servo, motor, battery holder ...) as a reference model with real mounting holes and ports, instead of modelling it. It is shown ghosted and left out of export and the wall check unless includeInExport. The answer gives the mounting holes and ports in model coordinates, so you can build posts and openings at the positions it reports. Use move to place it afterwards; combine cannot use a part as its target. Returns the new feature's id, which is also the body id.

part.description: Id of the part from list_parts, e.g. raspberry-pi-4b

variant.description: Id of a variant listed for that part (e.g. a servo size); omit for the standard one

position.description: Where the centre of the part's footprint goes (its lowest point is put on this z): [x, y, z] in mm. Z is up.

rotation.description: Rotation about X, then Y, then Z, around the footprint centre: [x, y, z] in degrees. Z is up.

includeInExport.description: Export and check the part like any body. By default it is a reference part: shown ghosted, left out of export, the wall check and volumes

tools.name: part_info
tools.description: Give the mounting holes (position, diameter, screw size, axis) and ports (facing, box) of a part already in the project, in model coordinates after any moves, and whether the library has newer dimensions. Use it to find where to put posts and openings.

id.description: Id of a part in the project (returned by add_part, or listed by get_project)

tools.name: add_sketch
tools.description: Add a 2D sketch on a base plane or on a flat face and draw shapes in it (rectangle, circle, line, polyline, arc, slot, polygon). For a face, give {body, select: {normal: "+z"}} (no list call needed) or {body, index, rebuildId} from list_faces. `offset` moves the plane along its normal (a plane floating 10 mm above XY, or 3 mm above a face). The sketch is solved and its remaining degrees of freedom reported. Use extrude or revolve to turn closed shapes into a solid.

plane.description: Base plane to sketch on. XY is the floor (sketch x = world X, y = world Y, normal up).

face.description: Sketch on a flat face of a body instead of a base plane: {body, index, rebuildId} with an index from list_faces, or {body, select: {...}} with a selector such as {"normal": "+z"}, which needs no list_faces call. The sketch's x, y axes and origin are the ones list_faces reports for that face.

body.description: Id of a body: the id of the feature that made it (returned by add_primitive, extrude, ...; listed by get_project)

rebuildId.description: The rebuildId reported by the list_faces / list_edges call that the indices came from. Indices are only valid for that exact model: if anything changed since, the command is refused and you must list again.

body.description: Id of a body: the id of the feature that made it (returned by add_primitive, extrude, ...; listed by get_project)

normal.description: A flat face facing that way: +z is the top, -z the bottom, +x the right side, -x the left, +y the back, -y the front

kind.description: Only flat or only curved faces

near.description: Take the matching face whose centre is nearest to this point: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

min.description: Lower corner: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

max.description: Upper corner: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

within.description: A box in model space (mm): the point tested (a face's centre or an edge's midpoint) must lie inside it, borders included

all.description: False (default): the selector must name one face, and several matches are refused with the candidates listed. True: take every matching face (shell can open several)

select.description: The flat face, e.g. {"normal": "+z"} for the top; one face (several matches are refused with the candidates listed)

offset.description: Move the sketch plane this far along its normal (XY: up, XZ: toward -Y, YZ: toward +X, a face: out of the body; negative goes the other way). Default 0. For a feature floating above a face or off the origin, without a slab or a move, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

x.description: X of the lower-left corner in the sketch plane, mm (the centre if centered is true)

y.description: Y of the lower-left corner in the sketch plane, mm (the centre if centered is true)

width.description: Size along the sketch's x axis, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

height.description: Size along the sketch's y axis, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

centered.description: True when x, y is the centre of the rectangle instead of its lower-left corner

radius.description: Radius, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

x1.description: X of the start point, mm

y1.description: Y of the start point, mm

x2.description: X of the end point, mm

y2.description: Y of the end point, mm

points.description: Corner points [x, y] in mm, in order. Horizontal and vertical segments get a horizontal / vertical rule.

closed.description: True joins the last point back to the first, so the shape can be extruded

radius.description: Radius, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

startAngle.description: Degrees counter-clockwise from the sketch's +x axis to the start of the arc

endAngle.description: Degrees counter-clockwise from the sketch's +x axis to the end; the arc runs counter-clockwise from the start

x1.description: X of the first end's centre, mm

y1.description: Y of the first end's centre, mm

x2.description: X of the second end's centre, mm

y2.description: Y of the second end's centre, mm

width.description: Width of the slot (the diameter of the round ends), in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

radius.description: Circumradius: distance from the centre to each corner, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

rotation.description: Degrees counter-clockwise the first corner is turned from the sketch's +x axis

shapes.description: Shapes to draw, in sketch coordinates (mm). Closed shapes can be extruded or revolved; shapes inside another become holes.

dimensions.description: True adds dimension rules (a size per rectangle side, circle and arc radius, slot width, polygon radius) so the sizes follow parameters, and pins each shape's anchor point. False draws free geometry.

name.description: Name for the sketch; defaults to Sketch 1, Sketch 2, ...

tools.name: extrude
tools.description: Extrude the closed shapes of a sketch into a solid: as a new body, or cut from / joined to an existing body. `start` moves where it begins off the sketch plane, `extent: throughAll` (with cut or join) runs it through the whole target, e.g. a through hole, and `extent: upToFace` with `until` stops at a flat face of a body, e.g. a post up to a lid. Returns the feature id (the new body's id when mode is new).

sketch.description: Id of the sketch to extrude (from add_sketch)

distance.description: How far to extrude. Needed unless extent is throughAll or upToFace, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

start.description: Where the extrusion begins, measured from the sketch plane along the direction it runs (default 0, at the sketch; negative starts behind it), in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

extent.description: distance (default) extrudes `distance` mm. throughAll runs through the whole target body in the direction (both ways when symmetric) and ignores distance; it needs mode cut or join, e.g. a through hole: sketch on the top face, direction backward, mode cut. upToFace stops at the flat face named by `until`, whatever the distance between (any mode; direction forward or backward), e.g. a post from a plate up to a lid's underside

until.description: With extent upToFace: the flat face of a body to stop at, {body, index, rebuildId} with an index from list_faces, or {body, select: {...}} such as {"normal": "-z"}. offset goes that far past the face along the direction (negative stops short). A tilted face gives a slanted end; a face behind the start or a curved face is refused.

body.description: Id of a body: the id of the feature that made it (returned by add_primitive, extrude, ...; listed by get_project)

rebuildId.description: The rebuildId reported by the list_faces / list_edges call that the indices came from. Indices are only valid for that exact model: if anything changed since, the command is refused and you must list again.

offset.description: How far past the face to go along the direction (default 0; negative stops short of it), in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

body.description: Id of a body: the id of the feature that made it (returned by add_primitive, extrude, ...; listed by get_project)

normal.description: A flat face facing that way: +z is the top, -z the bottom, +x the right side, -x the left, +y the back, -y the front

kind.description: Only flat or only curved faces

near.description: Take the matching face whose centre is nearest to this point: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

min.description: Lower corner: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

max.description: Upper corner: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

within.description: A box in model space (mm): the point tested (a face's centre or an edge's midpoint) must lie inside it, borders included

all.description: False (default): the selector must name one face, and several matches are refused with the candidates listed. True: take every matching face (shell can open several)

select.description: The flat face to stop at, e.g. {"normal": "-z"} for an underside; one face (several matches are refused with the candidates listed)

offset.description: How far past the face to go along the direction (default 0; negative stops short of it), in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

direction.description: forward goes along the sketch plane's normal, backward against it, symmetric half each way

mode.description: new makes a new body; cut removes the extrusion from `target`; join adds it to `target`

target.description: Body to cut or join. Defaults to the body a face sketch lies on, else the only body.

tools.name: revolve
tools.description: Revolve the closed shapes of a sketch about an axis in the sketch plane to make a solid of revolution: new body, or cut / join with an existing body. Use it for round parts: draw half the outline beside the axis.

sketch.description: Id of the sketch whose closed shapes are revolved (from add_sketch)

axis.description: Revolve about the sketch's own x or y axis (through its origin). Give this or axisLine.

axisLine.description: Or the id of a line in the sketch to revolve about (ids are listed in add_sketch's answer)

angle.description: How far to revolve, 0 to 360, in degrees, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

mode.description: new makes a new body; cut or join change `target`

target.description: Body to cut or join. Defaults to the body a face sketch lies on, else the only body.

tools.name: combine
tools.description: Boolean-combine bodies: union joins them into one body, subtract cuts the tools out of the target, intersect keeps what they share. To cut or intersect, the bodies must overlap: a cut that removes nothing is reported as a warning, an intersect with nothing shared fails. The target keeps its id; the tools are consumed. To hollow a body use shell, not a subtracted box; to check whether two bodies collide, use check_interference.

op.description: union joins the bodies into one (they need not touch); subtract cuts the tools out of the target; intersect keeps what they share. Subtract and intersect need the bodies to overlap

target.description: The body that stays (and keeps its id)

items.description: Id of a body: the id of the feature that made it (returned by add_primitive, extrude, ...; listed by get_project)

tools.description: Bodies combined into the target; they are consumed

tools.name: hole
tools.description: Drill a screw hole (M2 to M10, with clearance, tap or heat-set insert fit and optional counterbore / countersink) into a flat face. Name the face with a selector such as face {"normal": "+z"} (the top; no list call needed), or pass an index from list_faces together with its rebuildId. Use this for every screw, standoff or insert hole instead of cutting circles.

body.description: Id of a body: the id of the feature that made it (returned by add_primitive, extrude, ...; listed by get_project)

normal.description: A flat face facing that way: +z is the top, -z the bottom, +x the right side, -x the left, +y the back, -y the front

kind.description: Only flat or only curved faces

near.description: Take the matching face whose centre is nearest to this point: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

min.description: Lower corner: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

max.description: Upper corner: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

within.description: A box in model space (mm): the point tested (a face's centre or an edge's midpoint) must lie inside it, borders included

all.description: False (default): the selector must name one face, and several matches are refused with the candidates listed. True: take every matching face (shell can open several)

anyOf.description: Picks faces by what they look like or where they are, e.g. {"normal": "+z"} (the top), {"normal": "+x", "near": [40, 0, 5]} or {"kind": "curved", "all": true}. All given conditions must hold. Resolved when the command runs, so no list_faces call or rebuildId is needed.

face.description: The flat face the hole goes into (along its inward normal): an index from list_faces (then pass rebuildId), or a selector such as {"normal": "+z"} for the top, which needs no list_faces call. A selector that matches several faces is refused with the candidates listed: add near or within to narrow it.

rebuildId.description: Required when you give indices: the rebuildId reported by the list_faces / list_edges call they came from (indices are only valid for that exact model; if anything changed since, the command is refused and you must list again). Leave it out when you give a selector.

position.description: Centre of the hole [x, y] in mm in that face's sketch frame (list_faces gives each face's origin, axes and bounds2d). Defaults to a point on the face.

size.description: Screw size; the hole diameter comes from a clearance table

fit.description: close / normal / loose clearance, tap (drill for cutting a thread) or insert (heat-set insert)

head.description: none, or a counterbore / countersink for the screw head

depth.description: "through", or a blind depth in mm

allowance.description: Extra diameter in mm for printer tolerance

tools.name: add_text
tools.description: Put raised (emboss) or cut-in (engrave) text on a flat face: a name tag, a label, a part number. One line. size is the capital height in mm (4 mm or more prints clearly with a 0.4 mm nozzle). Change it later with update_feature (text, font, size, depth, mode, position, rotation, align).

body.description: Id of a body: the id of the feature that made it (returned by add_primitive, extrude, ...; listed by get_project)

normal.description: A flat face facing that way: +z is the top, -z the bottom, +x the right side, -x the left, +y the back, -y the front

kind.description: Only flat or only curved faces

near.description: Take the matching face whose centre is nearest to this point: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

min.description: Lower corner: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

max.description: Upper corner: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

within.description: A box in model space (mm): the point tested (a face's centre or an edge's midpoint) must lie inside it, borders included

all.description: False (default): the selector must name one face, and several matches are refused with the candidates listed. True: take every matching face (shell can open several)

anyOf.description: Picks faces by what they look like or where they are, e.g. {"normal": "+z"} (the top), {"normal": "+x", "near": [40, 0, 5]} or {"kind": "curved", "all": true}. All given conditions must hold. Resolved when the command runs, so no list_faces call or rebuildId is needed.

face.description: The flat face the text goes on: a selector such as {"normal": "+z"} (the top, no list call needed) or an index from list_faces with rebuildId. A selector that matches several faces is refused with the candidates listed: add near or within to narrow it.

rebuildId.description: Required when you give indices: the rebuildId reported by the list_faces / list_edges call they came from (indices are only valid for that exact model; if anything changed since, the command is refused and you must list again). Leave it out when you give a selector.

text.description: The words, on one line, up to 80 characters. Characters the font does not have are refused by name.

font.description: atkinson-hyperlegible-bold (clear sans, the default), sniglet-extrabold (round and bold), space-mono-bold (monospace, for part numbers), saira-stencil-one (stencil, for text cut all the way through) or archivo-black (thick and wide, for big labels)

size.description: Height of the capital letters, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

depth.description: How far the letters stand out (emboss) or are cut in (engrave), in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

mode.description: emboss raises the letters from the face, engrave cuts them into it

position.description: Where the line sits, [x, y] in mm in that face's sketch frame (list_faces gives each face's origin, axes and bounds2d): the middle of the line for align centre. Defaults to a point on the face.

prefixItems.description: X of the anchor, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"
Y of the anchor, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

rotation.description: Turn of the line, counter-clockwise looking at the face, in degrees, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

align.description: left, centre or right: which part of the line sits at position

tools.name: add_svg
tools.description: Put a logo, icon or drawing from SVG markup on a flat face as raised (emboss) or cut-in (engrave) shapes, or make it a body of its own (a plaque, a keychain: leave out body and face). Filled shapes become solids; lines are traced with round ends and corners; white shapes cut out what is under them. Text, pictures, clip paths, masks and gradients are left out and reported (convert text to paths first, or use add_text). Up to 300 outlines and 3,000 pieces. Give the SVG as its text (svg) or as the path of a .svg file on the user's computer (path). Change it later with update_feature (width, depth, mode, mirror, position, rotation).

svg.description: The SVG markup (the text of a .svg file), up to 2,000,000 characters. Shapes and lines are used; text, pictures, clip paths, masks and gradients are not (text must be converted to paths first). Leave out when you give path.

path.description: Absolute path of the .svg file on the user's computer (or one starting with ~), at most 2 MB, instead of svg. Example: C:\Users\me\Downloads\logo.svg or ~/Downloads/logo.svg

fileName.description: A name for the artwork, ending in .svg: it is shown in the feature's name

body.description: With face: the body the face is on. Leave out body and face to make the artwork a body of its own.

face.description: The flat face the artwork goes on: a selector such as {"normal": "+z"} (the top, no list call needed) or an index from list_faces with rebuildId. Leave out body and face to make the artwork a body of its own (a plaque, a keychain).

normal.description: A flat face facing that way: +z is the top, -z the bottom, +x the right side, -x the left, +y the back, -y the front

kind.description: Only flat or only curved faces

near.description: Take the matching face whose centre is nearest to this point: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

min.description: Lower corner: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

max.description: Upper corner: [x, y, z] in mm, Z up

within.description: A box in model space (mm): the point tested (a face's centre or an edge's midpoint) must lie inside it, borders included

all.description: False (default): the selector must name one face, and several matches are refused with the candidates listed. True: take every matching face (shell can open several)

anyOf.description: Picks faces by what they look like or where they are, e.g. {"normal": "+z"} (the top), {"normal": "+x", "near": [40, 0, 5]} or {"kind": "curved", "all": true}. All given conditions must hold. Resolved when the command runs, so no list_faces call or rebuildId is needed.

rebuildId.description: Required when you give indices: the rebuildId reported by the list_faces / list_edges call they came from (indices are only valid for that exact model; if anything changed since, the command is refused and you must list again). Leave it out when you give a selector.

width.description: Width of the artwork. Its height follows its shape. Default: 60% of the face, or 40 mm for a body of its own, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

height.description: Height of the artwork instead of its width (a plain number; the width follows its shape), in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

depth.description: On a face: how far the shapes stand out (emboss) or are cut in (engrave), default 1. As a body of its own: how thick it is, default 2, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

mode.description: emboss raises the shapes from the face, engrave cuts them into it. Ignored for a body of its own.

position.description: Where the middle of the artwork goes. On a face: [x, y] in mm in that face's sketch frame (list_faces gives each face's origin, axes and bounds2d), default the middle of the face. As a body of its own: [x, y] or [x, y, z] (the bottom on z), default [0, 0, 0].

prefixItems.description: X of the middle, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"
Y of the middle, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"
X of the middle, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"
Y of the middle, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"
Z of the bottom, in mm, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

rotation.description: Turn of the artwork, counter-clockwise looking at the face (from above for a body of its own), in degrees, a number or an expression over the project's parameters such as "width / 2 + 1"

mirror.description: Flip the artwork left to right before it is turned: for a stamp, or to read it from the other side

tools.name: fillet
tools.description: Round edges of a body with a radius. Name the edges with a selector such as edges {"direction": "z"} (the vertical edges) or {"onFace": {"normal": "+z"}} (the rim of the top), which needs no list call; or pass indices from list_edges together with their rebuildId. If it fails, the answer names the edges that broke it and the largest radius that works.

body.description: Id of a body: the id of the feature that made it (returned by add_primitive, extrude, ...; listed by get_project)

kind.description: Convex edges (outside corners) or concave ones (inside corners). Smooth edges (seams, tangent joins) are never taken

direction.description: Only straight edges parallel to this world axis; z picks the vertical edges

onFace.description: Only the edges around this face, e.g. {"normal": "+z"} for the edges of the top face

normal.description: A flat face facing that way: +z is the top, -z the bottom, +x the right side, -x the left, +y the back, -y the front

instructions:
Polypad is a parametric CAD editor. These tools build and inspect the model in the Polypad tab the user has open, and the user watches it change. Every change is one undo step for them.

Units and axes: lengths are millimetres, angles degrees, Z is up. Any length field accepts a number or an expression over the project's parameters ("width / 2"); prefer set_parameter for sizes that belong together.

Workflow:
1. Start with get_project to see what is already there (the user may have work open). new_project and open_project save the open project first, so nothing is lost: list_projects and open_project go back to earlier work. Still ask the user before switching away from a project they have open with features.
2. Build with add_primitive, or add_sketch then extrude / revolve. Ids returned by a command are the feature and body ids for later calls.
3. For hole, shell, fillet, chamfer and for sketching on a face, name the faces or edges with a selector instead of an index: face {"normal": "+z"} is the top, edges {"direction": "z"} are the vertical edges, edges {"onFace": {"normal": "+z"}} the rim of the top. A selector is resolved when the call runs, so you need no list call and no rebuildId. One that matches several faces where one is needed is refused with the candidates listed: add near [x, y, z] or within to narrow it. Only when no selector fits, call list_faces or list_edges and pass the indices together with the same rebuildId (it changes whenever the model changes; a stale one is refused with "Call list_edges again").
4. A feature that does not build stays in the project with its error: fix it with update_feature, or remove it with delete_feature or undo.
5. Check your work: measure gives volume and bounding box, and render_view returns a PNG (iso, top, front, right) so you can look at the result. Compare the numbers with what was asked before you finish.

Pick the tool by task:
- Hollow part (enclosure, box, cup): shell the solid with the open face(s) removed (faces {"normal": "+z"} opens the top); don't subtract a smaller box.
- Screw holes, standoffs, inserts: hole (size, fit close/normal/loose/tap/insert, counterbore or countersink, blind depth), not cut circles.
- Text, labels, name tags, part numbers: add_text on a flat face (emboss raises the letters, engrave cuts them in; size is the capital height in mm), not sketches of letters.
- Logos, icons and drawings (SVG): add_svg, on a flat face like add_text, or as its own body without body and face (a logo plaque, a keychain); not shapes traced by hand in sketches.
- Several of the same hole (a bolt circle on a flange, a row or grid of mounting holes): make one hole with hole, then pattern_hole with its id. For a bolt circle use layout kind circular, axis = the face normal axis (z for a top face), centre = a point on the circle's axis, count = number of holes; place the first hole on the circle itself (list_faces gives the face's frame and bounds). Copies that land off the face are skipped and reported.
- The same part again (four servos, two brackets): copy_body copies a body in one call (default: next to it along +X; give offset to place it). Rows, grids, around a circle, lattices: model one body, or one cutter body, then pattern it (then combine subtract for a cutter). Symmetric parts: model one side, then mirror.
- Boards, servos, motors and batteries: list_parts, then add_part (a reference model with real mounting holes and ports) instead of modelling them; build posts and openings at the positions it reports.
- Pockets, through holes and floating features (add_sketch + extrude): a pocket 3 mm deep: sketch on the top face (face selector {"normal": "+z"}), then extrude direction backward, distance 3, mode cut. A through-hole outline: the same with extent "throughAll" (no distance; it needs mode cut or join). A boss on a face: sketch on the face and extrude forward, mode join. A feature floating above a face or off the origin: add_sketch with offset (mm along the plane's normal: XY up, XZ toward -Y, YZ toward +X, a face out of the body), instead of a thin slab and a move. extrude's start begins the solid off the sketch plane (a boss that starts 2 mm above it). To stop at another body's face instead of a distance (a post from a plate up to a lid): extent "upToFace" with until {body, select: {"normal": "-z"}} naming the lid's underside (flat faces only; offset goes past it, negative stops short; direction forward or backward, not symmetric). Prefer these to building a cutter body and a combine.
- Round parts (knobs, turrets, finials, domes): add_sketch on XZ (sketch x = world X, sketch y = world Z), draw half the outline at x >= 0, then revolve with axis "y" (the world Z axis).
- Pipes, spacers and rings: the tube primitive (a torus for an O-ring), not two subtracted cylinders.
- A cylinder, cone, tube or torus lying along X or Y (a shaft, a pin, a rail): add_primitive with axis "x" or "y" (default "z", upright); never work out rotation signs. Without position it rests on the grid; with position that point is the centre of its base, so give z = its radius to rest it. get_project and measure report the axis.
- Sizes that belong together or may change: set_parameter first, then use the names in fields.
- Changing or fixing a feature: update_feature (or undo the last step); don't delete and rebuild.
- Picking edges and faces: use a selector (step 3). To look at the geometry near a point, list_faces and list_edges take near [x, y, z] (nearest first, with the distance, 20 rows by default), within {min, max} and limit, besides the filter.
- Fillet or chamfer fails: the answer names the edges that broke it and the largest radius or distance that works; set that value with update_feature (or use fewer edges).
- Saving the model for printing: export_file (STL or 3MF; STEP for other CAD programs). It saves into the user's Downloads folder unless you give a path, and tells you where. Bringing in an existing part: import_file with the file's absolute path, then combine, move or hole as usual.
- Parts meant for 3D printing: check_print (thin walls) and check_overhangs (faces that need support) before you finish, and fix what they name.
- Clearances, collisions and fits: check_interference on two bodies says whether they overlap, touch or stand apart; give clearance (mm per side) for parts meant to fit together (a lid in a box, a pin in a hole) and fix what it calls too tight. measure gives bounding boxes. Don't combine and undo to find out.

Results: a result with isError set was refused or something in the model did not build; the text says what and how to fix it. Nothing is changed by a refused call. A result may end with a line "Tip: ..." naming a better tool for what you just did; each tip is said once per session.
